bib.title: Dolma: an Open Corpus of Three Trillion Tokens for Language Model Pretraining Research
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), pages 15725-15788

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; Appendix O (all raw ablation result plots, Figures 13-92, text is axis ticks only) not read beyond captions and the start/end.

question: How can an open, documented, English 3T-token multi-source pretraining corpus be built, and which curation decisions (filters, dedup, mixing) improve models trained on it?
hypothesis: Evidence-backed curation choices (quality, content, dedup filters) improve downstream and perplexity results of models trained on the data; multi-source composition gives better domain fit than web-only corpora.
contributions: Release the Dolma Corpus, a diverse multi-source collection of 3T tokens across over 4B documents from 6 data sources.
Open source the Dolma Toolkit, a high-performance, portable tool to curate large datasets for language model pretraining.

method.summary: The authors build Dolma from Common Crawl, GitHub (The Stack), Reddit (Pushshift), peS2o papers, Project Gutenberg and Wikipedia/Wikibooks using a filter and mix toolkit, choosing each curation step by training 1.2B OLMo-style models on up to 150B tokens and comparing to a no-filter baseline. They then train OLMo-1B on the final corpus and compare it to other 1B models.
method.task: pretraining corpus construction; data ablations with next-token pretraining and zero-shot evaluation

datasets.name: Dolma v1.6 (output)
datasets.size: 3,059B Llama tokens; 4,367M documents; 11,519 GB UTF-8; 2,318B Unicode words (Table 1), from about 200 TB raw
datasets.preprocessing: language ID, quality, content, PII, dedup, decontamination per source

datasets.name: Dolma-Web (Common Crawl)
datasets.source: 25 Common Crawl snapshots 2020-05 to 2023-06 via CCNet; downloaded March 17-27 2023
datasets.preprocessing: FastText English score >= 0.5 (removes 61.7% of bytes); CCNet paragraph dedup (about 70% of paragraphs); URL dedup (53.2% docs); exact doc dedup (14.9%); Gopher rules + C4 NoPunc quality filters; FastText hate/NSFW sentence filter tau=0.4; regex PII; paragraph dedup (18.7% of paragraphs, 19.1% of characters in datasheet)

datasets.name: Dolma-Code (The Stack, dedup)
datasets.preprocessing: drop data-heavy extensions (csv, json, svg etc.) and assembly; RedPajama v1 and StarCoder heuristics; PII masking; detect-secrets removal

datasets.name: Dolma-Social (Reddit)
datasets.preprocessing: atomic content format; remove comments <500 chars, submissions <400 chars, docs >40,000 chars; remove comments with <3 votes; remove deleted/removed/over-18; 26,123 banned or NSFW subreddits excluded; toxicity filter; PII documents removed; doc-level dedup

datasets.name: peS2o (Semantic Scholar)
datasets.source: peS2o V2 derived from S2ORC, used as is (repetition filter in datasheet)

datasets.name: Project Gutenberg
datasets.preprocessing: English filter, drop pages under 25 words, title-match dedup

datasets.name: Wikipedia + Wikibooks (English and Simple)
datasets.source: Wikimedia dump of March 20 2023, CC BY-SA 4.0
datasets.preprocessing: WikiExtractor; drop documents with 25 or fewer words

datasets.name: C4 (supplement to web subset)
datasets.preprocessing: re-run through full web pipeline except URL dedup

datasets.name: Downstream eval suite (8 tasks)
datasets.source: ARC-E (and ARC-C offline), BoolQ, HellaSwag, OpenBookQA, PIQA, SciQ, WinoGrande

datasets.name: Paloma + Dolma held-out sets
datasets.source: perplexity suite (Magnusson 2023) plus RedPajama v1, RefinedWeb, Dolma 100 subreddits, Dolma 100 programming languages
datasets.preprocessing: paragraphs over 13 tokens found in Paloma removed (negligible: 0.001% characters)

training.objective: inferred: autoregressive next-token prediction (decoder-only language model)
training.optimizer: LionW for ablations; AdamW for OLMo-1B (switched due to LionW instabilities)
training.steps: max 95k (about 200B tokens) with runs stopped at 150B tokens (ablations); 739,328 (roughly 3.1T tokens) for OLMo-1B
training.tokens: up to 150B tokens per ablation; roughly 3.1T for OLMo-1B
training.hardware: 64 AMD Instinct MI250X accelerators (128 compute units in 16 nodes), micro-batch 8 per unit; OLMo-1B on 256 compute units; LUMI supercomputer
training.seeds: 5 random seeds for the code-mixture evaluation (Table 3); otherwise not stated

other.corpus_mix_for_OLMo_1B: not stated in this paper (no single mixture prescribed)

inference.samples: zero-shot ranked classification; bAbI and WebNLG in-context with 0-5 demonstrations over 5 seeds
inference.prompting: zero-shot in-context, each task cast as ranked text classification; prompts from PromptSource (Bach 2022), prompt truncation from Min et al. (2022); in-house harness similar to Eleuther harness

metrics.name: Paloma perplexity
metrics.definition: perplexity averaged over marked domains sampled equally per source

metrics.name: Exact match / Rouge-2
metrics.definition: exact match for bAbI and GSM8K, Rouge-2 for WebNLG

baselines: C4, mC4-en, RedPajama v1, RefinedWeb, Pile (1.2B models, 150B tokens)
eval.protocol: single run per ablation (seeds not stated), curves over training tokens; most ablation results only shown as plots (HellaSwag in main text, rest in Appendix O); no significance tests

evidence.quote: Due to instabilities we found in the LionW optimizer, we switched to using AdamW.

evidence.where: Section 5; the datasheet (N.3) says 'We decided to use the 24 most recent Common Crawl snapshots'

results.claim: Dolma totals about 3T Llama tokens across 6 sources, curated down from roughly 200 TB of raw text.
results.table: Table 1, row Total, column Llama tokens (billions)
results.note: Table says 4,367M documents; text says 'over 4B documents'

results.claim: Web data is 2,479B of Dolma's tokens; code 411B, Reddit 89B, papers 70B, books 6.0B, encyclopedic 4.3B.
results.table: Table 1, row Common Crawl, column Llama tokens (billions)

results.claim: Stacking quality filters, content filters and paragraph dedup compounds to improve 1.2B-model HellaSwag accuracy over an unfiltered baseline.
results.setup: 1.2B OLMo-style model, 150B tokens, Common Crawl pipeline, one run per config
results.quote: We show the positive compounding effect of all stages of our web pipeline on downstream model performance
results.note: magnitude only in Fig 3 plot, not stated in text

results.claim: Of the C4 and Gopher heuristics, C4 NoPunc alone beats C4 All and Gopher All, and Gopher All + C4 NoPunc is best.
results.quote: we find that C4 NoPunc on its own outperforms both C4 All as well as Gopher All on both perplexity and downstream tasks

results.claim: Gopher rules tag 15.23% of UTF-8 characters for removal.
results.quote: Gopher All tagged 15.23% of UTF-8 characters for removal, while C4 NoPunc tagged 22.73% of characters for removal.

results.claim: CCNet's KenLM Wikipedia-likeness buckets are unaffected by heuristic filtering, so model-based and heuristic quality filters are orthogonal.
results.quote: these buckets are often interpreted as high (21.9%), medium (28.5%), or low (49.6%) quality content

results.claim: The permissive toxicity threshold (tau=0.4) removes 5.5-7.3% of content but does slightly worse than the strict one (tau=0.0004, removes 29.1-34.9%); the authors chose the permissive one to keep the token count.
results.setup: FastText hate/NSFW classifiers on Jigsaw, 1.2B model ablation
results.note: the text calls tau=0.4 'High Threshold' and also 'more permissive'

results.claim: Quality, content and dedup filters overlap very little in which documents they remove, so their effects compound.
results.quote: Overall, we find that correlations are generally low, thus our filters select fairly different documents and are not redundant.

results.claim: Three-stage dedup: URL dedup removes 53.2% of documents, exact document dedup 14.9% of the rest, paragraph dedup 18.7% of paragraphs.
results.quote: Exact URL dedup filters 53.2% of documents.
results.note: datasheet reports paragraph dedup as 19.1% of UTF-8 characters, text reports 18.7% of paragraphs

results.claim: CCNet filters out 84.2% of Common Crawl content, from 175.1 TB to 27.7 TB.
results.quote: Overall, CCNet pipeline filters out 84.2% of the content in Common Crawl, from 175.1 TB to 27.7 TB.

results.claim: Treating Reddit comments and submissions as atomic independent documents beats partial or full thread linearization.
results.quote: treating submissions and comments as independent documents (Atomic Content) leads to better performance on our evaluation suite

results.claim: OLMo-1B averages 60.3 over 8 tasks, above TinyLlama (59.4) and Pythia (54.5), below StableLM2 (66.5).
results.setup: OLMo-1B (1.2B) trained roughly 3.1T tokens, zero-shot ranked classification
results.note: text says it outperforms TinyLlama in 4 of 8 tasks

results.claim: On Paloma perplexity, a model on multi-source Dolma matches the Pile model's curve and beats single-source C4, mC4-en and RefinedWeb models.
results.setup: 1.2B models on 150B-token samples of each corpus
results.quote: training on single-source corpora like C4, mC4 (English-only), and RefinedWeb leads to models with poor fit to diverse domains as indicated by higher average perplexity

results.claim: Adding code to the mix helps bAbI in-context learning: 0.0 exact match with 0% code, 8.8 with 5%, 10.1 with 15%.
results.setup: 1B models on C4 + Stack mixtures, 0-5 demonstrations, 5 seeds

results.claim: Fine-tuning on program-aided (PAL) GSM8K outputs gives 11.8 (0% code), 14.2 (5%) and 14.7 (15%); plain GSM8K gets 0.0 for all.
WebNLG Rouge-2 rises from 16.8 to 22.0 as code goes from 0% to 15%.
Reference+ (4.9% papers) and Gopher-like (24.2% papers) mixes reach nearly identical S2ORC perplexity, so a small share of in-domain data suffices.
results.setup: 1B models, four mixes in Table 4, no Reddit data in mixes
results.quote: despite significant differences in the amount of academic papers between Reference+ and Gopher-like (4.9% vs 24.2%), they achieve nearly identical results

results.claim: Code subset has tokenizer fertility 2.45 against 1.15-1.28 for other sources, because non-space whitespace becomes separate tokens.
results.setup: GPT NeoX tokenizer applied to each Dolma source
results.quote: which has a substantially higher fertility of 2.45

results.claim: 223 of 50,280 GPT NeoX vocabulary tokens (about 0.4%) never occur in Dolma.
Dolma contains whole copies of popular benchmark test sets: six PromptSource datasets are 100% contaminated and HumanEval, WiC, ESNLI, SNLI are over 90%.
results.setup: WIMBD analysis of Dolma against PromptSource datasets; mostly in the code subset
results.note: contaminated datasets are excluded from the downstream eval suite

results.claim: Decontaminating against Paloma removes only 0.003% of the dataset (v1.0, v1.5); v1.6 is not decontaminated.
results.quote: only 0.003% of our dataset is removed due to contamination with this evaluation set

results.claim: PII handling (replace if 5 or fewer spans, else drop document) affects 0.02% and 0.001% of documents and had no measurable effect on model performance.
results.setup: regex for emails, IPs, phone numbers; 25 Common Crawl snapshots
results.note: datasheet N.4 lists 0.05% tagged for masking and 0.11% for removal for the full filter, a different count

results.claim: Filtering speed in the toolkit is 122 CPU hours per TB when replicating the C4 recipe; the 200 TB raw set would take 5 days on a 192-vCPU c6a.48xlarge.
results.quote: our toolkit performed filtering at a rate of 122 CPU hours per TB

limits: English-only corpus; language ID false negatives leave a small share of non-English text.
Ablations use a single 1B-scale dense autoregressive transformer trained to 150B tokens; decisions may not hold at 7B-70B or other architectures.
Evaluation suite is small (8 tasks) and excludes contaminated tasks; effect of code on code generation cannot be measured until instruction tuning.
Most ablation outcomes appear only as plots (HellaSwag in main text, others in Appendix O) with single runs and no significance tests or stated seeds.
Manual inspection of the full corpus is infeasible; contents, quality and harms cannot be fully described.
Chose permissive toxicity threshold (tau=0.4) even though the stricter one scored better, to keep token count; PII uses regex that trades accuracy for speed.
Dolma v1.6 is not decontaminated; Dolma v1.7 later gave significant gains (per Conclusion), so this version has dated.
Pushshift Reddit data is no longer distributed; raw data is unavailable outside AI2 and Common Crawl raw text was not kept.
Training compute and wall clock for OLMo-1B are not stated; OLMo-1B's exact data mixture is not given here.
Snapshot count inconsistent: text says 25 Common Crawl snapshots, datasheet says 24.
